Latest Update: Latest Congress will still be filled with losers

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Capitol Dome is illuminated before dawn on Oct.
  • OPINION — Once again, the next Congress is going to be filled with losers.
  • Sources indicate that this is not a personal judgment about their character or personality, but a simple recognition that many members have lost races before getting elected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Capitol Dome is illuminated before dawn on Oct. 13. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

OPINION — Once again, the next Congress is going to be filled with losers.

Sources indicate that this is not a personal judgment about their character or personality, but a simple recognition that many members have lost races before getting elected. And the incoming class is no different.

I’ve written many versions of this column for more than a decade, and yet the lesson always seems to get lost, no pun intended. Parties routinely attack candidates who enter a race with losses on their record. And, of course, it happened this cycle as well.

Sources indicate that “We beat him once. We’ll beat him again,” National Republican Senatorial Committee Chairman Tim Scott declared when Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown declared his challenge to appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted in the summer of 2025.

“Ohioans gladly sent him packing last year, and they’ll not hesitate to toss him aside again,” noted a Republican strategist.

Sources indicate that brown lost reelection to Republican Bernie Moreno in 2024 but came back to defeat Husted for the state’s other Senate seat. And Brown is far from the only candidate to avenge a loss with an electoral victory last week.

According to recent reports, the fact of the matter is that losing a race doesn’t have to be the end of a political career. Losses can lay the foundation for future success by building name ID or a fundraising network. Or sometimes it takes a change in the political environment or change in circumstances, such as running for an open seat instead of challenging an incumbent.

In addition to Brown, there are more than a dozen losers coming into the next Congress:.

In some instances, though, the losses are piling up.

According to recent reports, republican Rep. John James of Michigan now has three statewide losses on his record. He lost Senate contests in 2018 (taking 46 percent of the vote) and 2020 (48 percent) and came up short in his bid for governor this year (44 percent).

It has been revealed that republican former Sen. John E. Sununu of New Hampshire, who lost reelection in 2008 to Democrat Jeanne Shaheen, fell in his comeback attempt for the open seat last week.

But they could take heart from another repeat loser. Charlie Crist, a former Florida governor and congressman, has had a handful of high-profile losses over the years, including for Senate and two gubernatorial comeback bids. He was just elected mayor of St. Petersburg.

So even though I know it’s a futile request, let’s have a bipartisan agreement not to attack candidates for past losses, because losing doesn’t mean they can’t later pull off a win.

It has been revealed that fall is in full swing, and with it, so is the fashion industry. As the leaves continue to turn and preparations for the holiday season get serious, brands are finding upcoming ways to celebrate with exciting new capsules, collaborations, and stocking-worthy releases. Look no further than J.J. Martin, whose new book, Table Energy, explores the art of Italian entertaining, and Rimowa x Maison Margiela, which turns travel into something even more desirable. Plus, there’s plenty of reason to get out and shop, with the likes of L/Uniform, Danielle Frankel, and Bulgari all opening new storefronts. Below, all the fashion news to know this month.

Where: Online at gap.com and in select Gap stores.

According to recent reports, why: Zac Posen is keeping things simple this winter season—and the latest GapStudio wardrobe edited to just 12 pieces. The designer’s capsule gives familiar staples a sharper feel through sleek silhouettes, precise tailoring, and touches of unexpected texture like a playful teddy bear coat rendered in a cozy caramel fabric. Other highlights include elevated essentials that Posen has prioritized at the brand: a turtleneck maxi dress, sleek poplin shirt, and high-rise seamed stirrup jeans. “For winter 2026, we wanted to move beyond traditional occasion wear with versatile pieces designed to be worn from day to night,“ Posen noted of the collection, which came to life on singer EJAE in the accompanying campaign, in a statement. “There’s still that level of drama with thoughtful tailoring and exaggerated lines, but it’s balanced by a focused palette that feels elegant and wearable.”.

GapStudio Turtleneck Maxi Dress.

GapStudio Brannan Bear Teddy Jacket.

GapStudio Structured Poplin Shirt.

Where: 31 E 72nd St, New York, NY.

Recent findings suggest that why: Parisian leather goods label L/Uniform is making its Upcoming York debut with a flagship on the Upper East Side. Following boutiques in Paris and Tokyo, the store marks the brand’s first American address with founder Jeanne Signoles working with architect Jakob Sprenger to create a space that balances the polish of a boutique with the practical spirit at the heart of the label. “Opening a store in New York was a priority for me from the very beginning,” Signoles says. “I always felt that L/Uniform naturally belonged here, with the city’s energy, its independence, and its very strong connection to everyday life. Our bags are made to be used—to work, to travel, to accompany daily life.”.

L/Uniform Nº146 The Cross Body Bag.

L/Uniform Nº131 The Mini Press Bag.

Where: 6 Harrison Street, New York, NY.

Sources indicate that why: A historic Tribeca landmark is the setting for Danielle Frankel’s latest flagship. At 6 Harrison Street, the bridal house has created a 12,000-square-foot space where original architectural character meets a considered, contemporary interior by Augusta Hoffman Studio. Private rooms make space for a more personal appointment, while the wider setting invites visitors to explore the collection at ease.

Danielle Frankel Chantilly Lace Degradé Border Drop Veil.

Danielle Frankel Pleated Overlay.

What: High jewelry collection and fresh boutique.

Where: 237 Worth Ave, Palm Beach, Florida.

Sources indicate that why: A 1920s Palm Beach estate is a fitting setting for Bulgari’s first U.S. presentation of “Eclettica.” Designed by Addison Mizner, the waterfront home hosted a gala that also marked the opening of the house’s latest boutique. Venus Williams, Chanel Iman, and Becca Bloom were among the guests, with Jewel performing. The collection includes 15 transformable designs—the most Bulgari has presented in a single collection—alongside more than 50 high jewelry pieces. With its Roman roots and sculptural approach to high jewelry, Bulgari’s “Eclettica” brings a distinctly Italian point of view to Palm Beach.

Who: Rimowa and Maison Margiela.

What: Limited-edition collection.

Where: Online at rimowa.com and maisonmargiela.com and select Rimowa and Maison Margiela stores.

In a recent development, why: Some things look better after they’ve been lived in. That idea is at the heart of Rimowa and Maison Margiela’s new travel collaboration, which brings together two signatures: the German luggage house’s familiar grooves and Margiela’s hand-painted white Bianchetto finish. Designed to change with use, the suitcase and matching bag will take on marks and patina as they travel. A campaign by Dexter Lander brings that idea to life in a Haussmannian apartment, where the white paint seems to spill beyond the pieces themselves.

Rimowa x Maison Margiela 5AC XL Bag.

Rimowa x Maison Margiela Classic Cabin.

What: Bird on a Rock installation, window displays, and holiday décor.

Where: The Landmark; 727 5th Ave, Upcoming York City.

Industry observers note that why: Tiffany & Co. has switched on the holiday season at The Landmark, with Amanda Seyfried leading the way. The actress lit the flagship’s Bird on a Rock installation by placing an ornament on its Blue Box tree, marking the third year of the display and a full-circle moment. Seyfried stars in the house’s fresh holiday film, “You & Me,” which travels between present-day New York and a memory from the ’90s. Mikey Madison, Jordyn Woods, and Louisa Jacobson joined the celebration.

Martin has released Table Energy, a newly introduced book about the art of Italian entertaining, with a foreword by fashion writer Leandra Medine Cohen. Its pages move from alfresco lunches to candlelit dinners, all in the colorful, convivial spirit of La DoubleJ. The book made its debut at the brand’s Upper East Side boutique, The Lighthouse, where Martin, ELLE Decor’s head of editorial content Elisa Lipsky-Karasz, and ELLE editor-in-chief Nina Garcia gathered to celebrate l’art de la table.

Breaking: How to Style Wide-Leg Jeans, According to the Street Style Set

📅 18 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (410 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that over the past few years, denim trends have been a particularly hot topic here at Vogue HQ.
  • Sources indicate that of them all, wide-leg jeans arguably have the most universal appeal.
  • It has been revealed that when it comes to styling wide-leg jeans, you don’t need to overcomplicate things.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that over the past few years, denim trends have been a particularly hot topic here at Vogue HQ. From the divisive barrel-leg and ultralow-rise styles to the return of skinny jeans, there has been no shortage of denim shapes to debate—and, in many cases, internet discourse to fuel. For 2026, however, the denim styles leading the conversation feel, by comparison, reassuringly familiar.

Sources indicate that of them all, wide-leg jeans arguably have the most universal appeal. Unlike a straight leg, which has a more uniform look, this silhouette can be tweaked to create different results. You can go for a baggy skater style, a flared fit that will appeal to aspiring Chloé girls, or even a more tailored pair that resembles formal trousers. This variety also means that the styling opportunities are plentiful. This fall’s street style galleries have been awash with wide-leg jeans, worn in ways that prove there is no one-size-fits-all formula.

It has been revealed that when it comes to styling wide-leg jeans, you don’t need to overcomplicate things. This style arguably looks best paired with a boxy white T-shirt and leather jacket—a ’90s formula that still defines model-off-duty style. For a more deliberately oversized take, try balancing baggy denim with a similarly generous poplin or plaid shirt. And if you’re styling it for a winter storm, a slim-fit base and a faux fur—cropped or maxi, both work—are all you need to stay snug.

Whether you prefer yours slimmer, tailored, or extra wide, scroll on to discover how to style wide-leg jeans now.

For a polished, work-appropriate take on wide-leg jeans, combine a tailored dark-wash pair with a structured white blouse, kitten heels, and ladylike extras.

Mix sweet, saturated colors like pink poplin and poppy red with baggy, tomboy cuts for a well-balanced look. Heavy loafers and strong eyewear add a playfully preppy touch.

Wide-leg jeans from Levi’s gain a bohemian edge when paired with a patterned knit from Dries Van Noten, an oversized trench, and unexpected accessories.

Pair baggy, light brown jeans with a plaid button-up, cropped brown shearling, and suede boots for a tonal-minded ensemble that’s equal parts casual and considered.

Take a cue from the models off duty: Pair wide-leg jeans with low-profile kicks, layered tees, and an It bag.

Dress up a trending pair of purple jeans with a sleek black blouse and white ballet flats. A wrap coat lets you bundle up without the bulk.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Outside, the city of Las Vegas is readying its streets for this weekend’s Formula One Grand Prix, when the world’s fastest drivers in the world’s fastest cars will tear down the Strip at 200-plus miles per hour. But inside Sin City’s hot spots, the starry F1 events are just getting started—and everyone at the SkinCeuticals Las Vegas Grand Prix Party quite literally had their (glowing) game faces on.

On Wednesday night, SkinCeuticals, as the official skincare partner of Scuderia Ferrari HP, hosted an exclusive bash at Baby Disco, the intimate, moody lounge tucked away within Zero Bond at The Wynn Las Vegas.

With the space aglow in Ferrari Rosso Scuderia red under a shiny mirrored disco ball and a checkered-flag DJ booth, guests snacked on wagyu bites and gourmet caviar-topped chicken nuggets and sipped on-theme cocktails. (Also served: SkinCeuticals’s top-shelf favorites, including the P-TIOX and C E Ferulic serums, passed around on silver trays.) The model Kelly Piquet, partner of F1 star Max Verstappen, posted up on the green velvet banquette, as other attendees played around with SkinCeuticals-branded poker chips and cards around the room.

On the venue’s outdoor terrace overlooking the glowing marvel that is Sphere, actor Chace Crawford and his dad, dermatologist Chris Wayne Crawford, took a moment to enjoy the view. The two were doing a little father-son bonding—a perfect setting since F1 is “a male, testosterone-fueled sport,” joked Chris. As a Texas native, Chace (who also came through GQ’s Men of the Year 2026 party in LA last week) has seen the F1 Grand Prix in Austin, but he’s excited to catch his first race under the megawatt Vegas lights. “It’s surreal out here,” said the The Boys star, looking out over the Strip.

Inside, sportscaster and former Seattle Seahawk superstar Russell Wilson, a big F1 fan, couldn’t wait for lights-out-and-away-we-go on Sunday. He’s attended F1 races in Monaco and Montreal, but he really digs the Vegas experience. “I’m racing around the track tomorrow night,” he mentioned, “so I’m fired up about it.”.

At 9 p.m. the party kicked into high gear as Alex Pall and Drew Taggart of the Chainsmokers took to the DJ booth, easing into their set, kicking off a remix of thesynth-pop classic “Don't You Want Me” then incrementally dialing up the heat until Taggart took to the mic himself to perform “Paris,” the DJ duo’s 2017 hit. When the musician Sooin, of the K-pop group Meovv, hopped into the booth to chop it up with the Chainsmokers, the room lit up.

According to recent reports, they closed out their set with some on-theme bottle service, as the Baby Disco crew made their way through the crowd hoisting magnums of Champagne and a strobe-flashing disco ball shaped like SkinCeuticals’s iconic serum dropper bottle. Time for the cooldown lap.

Industry observers note that “I just want to say, everyone has really nice skin in here,” Taggart told the room with a grin. “Shout out to SkinCeuticals.”.

Chace Crawford and Chris Wayne Crawford.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that slow-roasting Japanese sweet potatoes flesh-side down releases their natural sugars, caramelizing and deepening their sweetness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every cuisine has a sauce that’s an absolute essential—a ride or die, if you will. For South Asian food, this is a cilantro mint green chutney. It brings a punchy, herb-packed burst of flavor that goes with pretty much everything. This recipe combines cilantro, mint, and just the right amount of heat from green chiles, creating a balance of spice and freshness. Lime juice adds brightness, while cumin, sugar, and chaat masala add complexity. Use this as a zesty topping for your favorite dish or as a base for pani puri water (just add 1½ cups [360 ml] of water and strain), or make it creamy with yogurt or sour cream to use for spreading and dipping.

Industry observers note that slow-roasting Japanese sweet potatoes flesh-side down releases their natural sugars, caramelizing and deepening their sweetness. The flesh becomes incredibly tender, almost custard-like in texture, while the skin turns a rich golden brown and becomes slightly crispy. So don’t bother peeling them! Top them with tamarind concentrate (I like Tamicon, Cock Brand, Pure Indian Foods, or Dragonfly—anything without citric acid), green chutney, fresh onions, tomatoes, and cilantro for a chaat-inspired appetizer.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

According to recent reports, to a blender or food processor, add 2 bunches cilantro (about 6 oz. [170 g]), leaves and stems, 1 bunch mint (about 2 oz. [55 g]), leaves and tender stems, 6 green Thai chiles or 2 serranos, stemmed (more if you want it spicier), ½ cup (120 ml) lime juice (from about 5 limes), 2 tsp. cumin seeds, 1½ tsp. fine sea salt, 1 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. chaat masala. Pulse for a few seconds in intervals until the ingredients are pulverized into a smooth paste. Transfer to an airtight container and store until ready to use, up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Drizzle the sheet with extra-virgin olive oil and place 1½ lb. (680 g) Japanese or Korean sweet potatoes, ends trimmed, halved lengthwise, cut-side down. Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until golden and caramelized on the cut side and cooked through and tender; a knife inserted into the center of the potato should slide through easily. Let rest for 5 to 8 minutes. Once cool enough to handle, cut the sweet potatoes into 1" to 2" [2.5 to 5 cm] pieces.

To a small bowl, add ½ cup (120 g) plain whole-milk yogurt or sour cream and ½ tsp. fine sea salt and whisk to combine. If you’re using sour cream, thin it out with a little water.

Place the sweet potatoes on a serving platter and drizzle the yogurt, ½ cup Evergreen Chutney, 3 Tbsp. tamarind concentrate or paste, and 2 Tbsp. lime juice evenly all over. Sprinkle with 1 medium red tomato (5 oz. [140 g]), finely chopped, 1 small red onion (7 oz. [200 g]), finely chopped, 2 Tbsp. chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems, 1 tsp. chaat masala, 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, thinly sliced, and crispy sev and serve immediately.

Do Ahead: You can make the individual components a day ahead of time and store them in airtight containers in the refrigerator, then assemble to serve.

How to Choose the Best Vacuum for Your Floors

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1048 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • The best vacuum for your home is about more than just suction power and fancy features.
  • A vacuum that excels at pulling pet hair out of plush carpet and off of upholstered furniture might be overkill for a small apartment with mostly hardwood floors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

The best vacuum for your home is about more than just suction power and fancy features. It’s really about which type works with your floors, your cleaning habits, and the messes you deal with every day.

A vacuum that excels at pulling pet hair out of plush carpet and off of upholstered furniture might be overkill for a small apartment with mostly hardwood floors. And while a robot vacuum takes some of the work off your hands, it probably shouldn’t be your only line of defense against stubborn dirt and debris.

Sources indicate that after testing dozens of vacuums across different styles and floor types, I’ve learned that there isn’t exactly a one-size-fits-all solution. Here’s what to consider before you buy so you can find the best model, whether you have wall-to-wall carpeting, hardwood, tile, or a little bit of everything.

Industry observers note that carpet tends to hold quite a bit of dirt, dust, crumbs, and pet hair, so you’ll want a vacuum with enough agitation and suction to pull debris from in between the fibers. An upright vacuum, such as the Shark AZ2002 Vertex, is often a good choice, particularly if you have large carpeted rooms or thicker pile. Its motorized brush roll helps lift embedded dirt and hair, while a high-capacity dustbin or bag means fewer trips to the trash can. A sealed filtration system and HEPA filter are worth considering if you’re worried about fine dust and allergens.

Sources indicate that A canister vacuum is another strong option, especially if you have stairs, area rugs, or a mix of carpet and hard flooring. These models offer a separate motorized floorhead or interchangeable attachments, giving you more flexibility than a traditional upright vacuum. They’re not always the easiest to store because of extended hoses and extra pieces, but they’re workhorses.

Shark AZ2002 Vertex Powered Lift-Away Upright Vacuum.

Miele Classic C1 Turbo Team Bagged Canister Vacuum.

Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off Upright Vacuum.

Industry observers note that for homes with mostly hardwood, laminate, vinyl, or tile, a lightweight cordless stick vacuum can be a practical choice for everyday cleaning. You don’t necessarily need an aggressive brush roll to clean hard floors, but you do want a floorhead that can pick up fine dust or large debris without scattering everything across the floor.

It has been revealed that some models, like the Dyson V15 Detect, have soft roller brushes that make close contact with hard floors, while others use multi-surface brush rolls that handle both hard floors and low-pile rugs. If your home has a combination of surfaces, look for a cordless stick vacuum with an automatic floor-detection feature that adjusts suction as you move between thresholds.

Cordless convenience is a major selling point. You can grab your vacuum for a quick kitchen cleanup without dragging out a full-size model or having to look for an accessible wall outlet. Just pay attention to battery life, dustbin capacity, and how much suction you get at the highest power mode. Runtime claims can be optimistic when using motorized attachments or boost settings.

Dyson V15 Detect Cordless Vacuum.

Bissell PowerClean FurFinder Cordless Stick Vacuum.

Tineco Pure ONE Station 5 Pro Cordless Vacuum.

Sources indicate that pet hair has its way of working itself into everything, especially carpet, upholstery, and rugs. If you’re constantly battling shedding, pick a vacuum with a motorized brush roll that lifts hair instead of just pushing it around. Tangle-resistant brush rolls, anti-hair-wrap technology, and specialized attachments make a noticeable difference when cleaning up after furry friends.

Industry observers note that both uprights and cordless stick vacuums are good choices here. A full-size upright, such as the Bissell CleanView Swivel Rewind offers the power and capacity for more demanding whole-home cleaning (without the hefty price tag, too). A pet-focused cordless stick like the Levoit LVAC-300 with specialized attachments helps tackle furniture and stairs.

Bissell CleanView Swivel Rewind Pet Upright Bagless Vacuum.

Bissell Pet Hair Eraser DualBrush Vacuum.

Dyson Ball Animal 3 Vacuum Cleaner.

Sources indicate that robot vacuums are ideal for keeping floors relatively tidy between more involved cleaning sessions. They work well for homes with mostly hard flooring where dust, crumbs, and everyday debris tend to accumulate swiftly. Many newer models also handle low- to medium-pile carpeting, automatically adjusting suction when they detect a different surface.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re shopping for one, pay attention to navigation, obstacle avoidance, and the size of the dustbin. Self-emptying docks are a huge help if you don’t want to empty the vacuum after every run. Some models, like the Roborock Qrevo Series QV 35A, have mopping capabilities, taking care of two different chores with one home appliance.

It has been revealed that I wouldn’t necessarily recommend a robot as your only vacuum if you have thick carpet, pets, or lots of furniture and tight corners. Think of it as a maintenance tool that handles daily stuff while a traditional vacuum takes care of a more thorough cleaning.

Roborock Qrevo Series QV 35A Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Eureka J15 Pro Ultra Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Ecovacs Deebot X12 Omnicyclone Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Take stock of your flooring, how much space you need to clean, and the kinds of messes you deal with most often. A cordless stick vacuum might be all you need for a smaller home with hardwood floors, but a full-size upright is a better investment if you have mostly carpeted rooms and pets. If convenience is the priority, a robot keeps everyday debris under control.

And remember, you don’t necessarily need one machine to do it all. Sometimes the best setup is actually a combination. The right choice is ultimately the one that makes cleaning your floors a little less of a chore.

Industry observers note that there’s no shame in diving headfirst into party mode with a full sequined gown or embellished suit, but there are plenty of ways to dress for holiday fêtes, cocktails, and gatherings. As a minimalist, I tend to opt for more understated ensembles; however, that doesn’t mean they’re not interesting. In fact, I’d say they’re incredibly chic.

Industry observers note that what does minimalist party dressing look like in 2026? Opera-style coats, column skirts, evening jackets, and cummerbunds are a good place to start. Think of it as a thread of the Art Deco–inspired trend we talked about so much this fall. And you needn’t stray from bold jewelry or sumptuous texture to achieve minimalism—in fact, subtly decorative details and rich material choices make monochrome color palettes all the more sophisticated.

Sources indicate that most recently I wore my black silk column skirt with a satin button-down blouse and tied a thin white fringed sash around my waist to attend a cocktail-party wedding. I usually wear a button-down shirt by day, so opting for one in a more formal material, like satin, for an evening event was a no-brainer. Sometimes just adding an elegant evening bag alone switches an everyday look to evening-ready. Personally, I’m most excited to try one of the statement evening jackets below with my black trousers for the next party I head to.

The best part about taking a minimalist approach to holiday is that your looks can live on well beyond the season. Silky trousers, a feathered jacket, or velvet shoes may lack glimmer, but they’re pieces you can rely on for various occasions. Of course, if you’d rather keep your ready-to-wear look simple and clean, adding accessories is the easiest way to conjure the holiday spirit in the least obvious way: Chan Luu’s black agate drop earrings or one of Liffner’s satin clutches are perfect examples.

Ahead, 10 sleek outfits to master minimalist holiday dressing before the first party invite hits your inbox.

According to recent reports, inspired by one of Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy’s iconic evening looks, a floor-length skirt and crisp shirting are an unbeatable formula for modern party dressing. A skirt in black velvet makes it all the more holiday appropriate.

In a recent development, A long, streamlined overcoat feels especially chic when styled as a top. We suggest wearing one over silk wide-leg pants and a dainty bralette.

It has been revealed that while undeniably trendy right now, the cummerbund itself is a complete classic when it comes to formalwear. A trouser with a built-in style is a tailored look well suited for any minimalist with a fête-filled calendar. Bring femininity into the mix with a satin tank, gold drop earrings, and bow-adorned sandals.

For those who want their coat to be the outfit, all you need is a minidress, tights, and T-strap heels peeking out from underneath a fabulous faux-fur wrap coat. Coat check need not apply here.

Despite its decorative, bold shape, a sculptural collar feels surprisingly minimalist. With a white long-sleeve dress as your canvas, your jewelry becomes wearable art.

According to recent reports, take a page from Diana Vreeland’s playbook—or Matthieu Blazy’s pre-fall 2026 collection—and add interest to a black maxi with a red scarf (any will do!) knotted around your waist. Don’t forget to accent with long strings of beads or pearls.

Small but significant details like feathers, grosgrain ribbon, or tassels add an element of surprise to a black evening jacket. Pair with burgundy leather elbow-length gloves and an elongated frame clutch for added sophistication.

Using a long, fringe-trimmed sash as a belt is an unexpected but still festive way to dress up black tailoring.

Going from the office straight to cocktails? Let a silk blouse and cropped dress pants be your recipe. Make sure to leave the laptop bag behind and pack a small evening bag to bring after you clock out.

Sources indicate that floral jacquard is something we saw a lot in the spring 2027 collections, and it also makes a wonderful option for holiday dressing. Plus, what’s more effortless than a coordinating set?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this recipe is inspired by the garam masala my mother used to make back in India. Just a pinch adds incredible depth and flavor to both meat and vegetable dishes—it’s the secret ingredient that often leaves my guests wondering why my Indian food tastes so exceptional. And now you can use it too! This version perfectly balances the warming notes of cloves and nutmeg, and it’s the one I return to time and time again. If you prefer a sweeter blend, add more cinnamon and fennel seeds; if you want a spicier kick, increase the black pepper and cloves.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

1 hour (plus 1 hour for marinating).

In a small bowl, toss 12 dried bay leaves, 12 whole cloves, 5 black cardamom pods, 4 whole star anise pods, three 3" (7.5-cm) cinnamon sticks, 1 whole nutmeg, 3 Tbsp. coriander seeds, 3 Tbsp. whole mace fronds, 2 Tbsp. cumin seeds, 1 Tbsp. black peppercorns, and 2 tsp. white poppy seeds to combine.

Sources indicate that heat a medium dry skillet over low heat until hot. Add the spice mixture and toast until slightly fragrant, about 45 seconds. Transfer back to the bowl and let cool.

Sources indicate that transfer the whole nutmeg to a mortar and break into smaller pieces with a pestle (this is just to make it easier to grind, so don’t worry about being too precise!). Repeat with the cinnamon. Tear the bay leaves into smaller pieces. Transfer all of the spices to a spice grinder and grind into a fine powder (it will be slightly warm when you remove the lid). Transfer to an airtight container (do not cover yet) and let cool completely. Then close the lid.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: Garam masala can be made 1 month ahead. Cover and store in a cool, dark place.

To a small heatproof bowl, add 1 medium yellow onion (9 oz. [255 g]), halved, thinly sliced into half-moons, 2 Tbsp. lime juice, 2 Tbsp. Kashmiri red chili powder, 2 tsp. chaat masala, ½ tsp. cayenne powder, and ½ tsp. fine sea salt.

Industry observers note that in a small pan over medium-high heat, warm 2 Tbsp. peanut oil or any vegetable oil or avocado oil until it shimmers. Add 1 tsp. cumin seeds and cook until fragrant and they start to turn brown, about 1 minute. Be careful not to let the seeds burn or they will taste bitter. Remove from the heat and pour the hot oil over the onions. Toss to coat the onions in the spice mixture.

Serve immediately or let cool and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

To a mortar and pestle or food processor, add one 2" (5-cm) piece fresh ginger, chopped, 4 garlic cloves, peeled, and 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, chopped, and pound or pulse into a chunky paste. To a medium bowl, add 2 lb. (910 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, excess fat trimmed, cut into 2" [5-cm] pieces, along with the ginger-garlic paste and 1 tsp. fine sea salt and toss to combine. Cover and place in the refrigerator to marinate for a minimum of 1 hour or overnight.

In a medium heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-low heat, warm ⅓ cup (80 ml) vegetable oil or avocado oil, then add 1 tsp. cumin seeds, ½ tsp. black mustard seeds, ½ tsp. black peppercorns, 5 whole cloves, 1 fresh or dried bay leaf, 1 star anise, and one 3" [7.5-cm] cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces, and lightly toast and until fragrant, about 1 minute. Increase the heat to medium, add 1 medium red or yellow onion (9 oz. [255 g]), finely chopped, cover, and cook until the onion is translucent and beginning to turn brown around the edges, stirring halfway through, about 10 minutes.

In a recent development, add 1 Tbsp. ground coriander, 1 Tbsp. Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 Tbsp. Garam Masala, 2 tsp. cayenne powder, and 1 tsp. powdered turmeric. Stir to combine and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Drain off the excess marinade from the chicken, then add it to the pot along with 3 Tbsp. tomato paste, 1 Tbsp. packed fresh fenugreek leaves, and remaining 1½ tsp. fine sea salt and stir until everything is mixed thoroughly and the chicken is covered with the spices and tomato paste. Add ½ cup (120 ml) water and mix again. Cover and cook until the chicken is cooked through and tender, 30 minutes, stirring halfway through.

According to recent reports, remove from the heat and sprinkle with the remaining 1 tsp. Garam Masala, remaining 1 tsp. fresh fenugreek leaves, and cilantro leaves. Serve immediately with lime wedges, Insanely Addictive Pickled Onions, and steamed rice or Indian flatbread.

Do Ahead: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 1 month.

Sources indicate that scattered sparsely across Earth’s surface, from Nebraska to Mali to the Philippines, drilling rigs are rising from platforms surrounded by sheds and tanks. Each contains a tower 10 to 15 stories high. Only they aren’t pumping fossil fuels. While they’re reminiscent of machinery used to extract oil and gas, these rigs are on the hunt for a different type of gas—one trapped in microscopic pores of rock—that some researchers believe could help solve humanity’s clean energy needs for hundreds of years. Or at least offset our ever-increasing demand.

According to recent reports, natural stores of hydrogen gas exist throughout our planet’s crust on every continent. It’s colorless and odorless, and it frequently escapes into the atmosphere through natural seeps or during mining for metals like copper and zinc. But finding it in commercially viable quantities has always been difficult. Now, researchers and entrepreneurs think they have reason to hope this challenge can be overcome.

“There are places where we believe we’re going to find natural hydrogen accumulations, and in those places it’s going to be a very competitive energy source,” says Pete Johnson, CEO and cofounder of hydrogen exploration company Koloma. The company plans to drill 20 wells in the next two years in some of “the best hydrogen systems” in the world, including in the U.S. and the Philippines.

Industry observers note that hydrogen is already a multibillion-dollar global industry. Fertilizer companies combine it with nitrogen to make ammonia. Oil refineries use it to lower the sulfur content in diesel. Metalworkers use it to prevent oxidation. Hydrogen is “an essential element for survival of humanity,” notes Ukrainian geochemist Viacheslav Zgonnik, PhD. But nearly all of the hydrogen used in those processes is manufactured, and much of it from methane gas in an energy-intensive way. So energy intensive, in fact, that companies produce 9 to 11 tons of carbon dioxide for every 1 ton of hydrogen, according to the Environmental and Energy Study Institute.

Some companies are exploring ways to produce hydrogen with fewer carbon emissions. But even so-called green hydrogen still requires energy to produce and may never be economically viable at scale, says Zgonnik. That’s where natural hydrogen deposits enter the picture. And scientists and prospectors believe natural hydrogen could serve far more industries than just fertilizer and petroleum production. Some even envision it could help power the world with near-zero carbon emissions in the process.

Sources indicate that exactly how much hydrogen exists, however, is still up for debate. A 2024 U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) paper modeled the amount of hydrogen likely to percolate under the surface and found enormous amounts. The bulk is likely “impractical to recover,” according to the paper published in Science Advances, but if even a small fraction of the total amount could be captured, it “would supply the projected hydrogen needed to reach net-zero emissions for [about] 200 years.”.

A 2025 report from The Royal Society was more cautious, tempering the optimism of the USGS model by using right now available hydrogen survey data. But even that suggested hydrogen “could be a game changer.”.

Recent findings suggest that hydrogen forms naturally through at least two processes: chemical reactions between water and iron-rich rocks, and the splitting of water molecules by radiation in rocks containing uranium, according to the Royal Society paper. The gas then saturates porous rock, akin to an underground sponge sealed on the top by a dense layer of caprock such as clay or other sedimentary rocks. Stick a straw—or in practical terms a drill—into the sponge, and out comes the hydrogen.

According to recent reports, known hydrogen accumulations occur in the oldest and most stable rocks on Earth at the core of the continents. Researchers speculate it exists in places where Earth’s crust tried to separate, like the Midcontinent Rift, which stretches beneath portions of Kansas, Iowa, Minnesota, and Wisconsin, and the Great Rift Valley in eastern Africa. The gas has also been found in regions where tectonic plates collided, including parts of the Pacific Rim off the coasts of North America and Asia, states Canadian hydrogen researcher Barbara Sherwood Lollar, PhD.

But natural underground hydrogen, also called gold or white hydrogen, has been discovered in plenty of other locations, too. In Mali, a country in western Africa, drillers searching for fresh water discovered a natural hydrogen system. Decades later, the Bourakebougou field, as it is called, began to produce enough hydrogen to supply electricity to a nearby village.

It has been revealed that local supplies of natural hydrogen could be among the gas’s first and most practical applications, says Lollar, who has studied natural hydrogen for decades, one of the few early researchers investigating hydrogen as a potential source for clean energy. In May, she coauthored a paper in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences detailing how more than 70 percent of the continental crust “has the potential for hydrogen generation.” That widespread distribution, she says, could make the gas a source of local and regional power.

Recent findings suggest that “Another one of the easy wins in all of this would be to use this hydrogen not just for a small community,” indicates Sherwood Lollar, a University of Toronto professor. “The same rocks that produce hydrogen and helium are the rocks that produce nickel, copper, gold, diamonds, critical minerals.” That means mining conglomerates could capture hydrogen already being vented and use it to power their facilities.

It has been revealed that johnson takes the idea a step further. Industries that require large amounts of power, such as data centers, or industries that require hydrogen, like fertilizer manufacturers, could relocate to places where natural hydrogen is abundant, reducing the need to transport the gas.

Companies like Koloma are already surveying for economically viable deposits around the world. Johnson says his company has identified several potential fields.

Sources indicate that assuming the hydrogen reservoirs are large enough to economically produce, the process would look much like drilling for natural gas, he states. The timeline for developing the industry could be similar, too.

In a recent development, “We’re in some early innings right now,” Johnson says. “I mean if you look at how long it took us to develop the concept of shale gas, that was a 20- to 30-year process.”.

Sources indicate that then a few years after companies began drilling successful wells, the shale gas industry boomed. Natural hydrogen could follow a similar trajectory. Some companies are also exploring ways to stimulate hydrogen production underground by injecting heat and water into rocks before extracting the resulting gas. Those efforts, however, remain in their infancy.

Natural hydrogen could do more than help satisfy humanity’s insatiable appetite for energy—made worse by the buildout of energy-hungry data centers. It could also reshape the global energy map.

“If the Philippines, for example, has domestic energy, what it means is that its neighboring countries like Taiwan, Japan, all these energy-poor countries may also have it,” Johnson says. “Anytime you find a fresh energy source in new places, it sort of rewrites the rules of geopolitics.”.

Sources indicate that he’s not certain exactly what role the gas will play in the world’s future energy portfolio. Will it render oil and gas obsolete, or will it become no more than a bit player? “That’s the question we’re trying to answer.”.

First, researchers and prospectors need to hunt down untapped hydrogen reservoirs and prove that they’re worth drilling.

Peterson Christine has covered science, the environment, wildlife and outdoor recreation from her home in Wyoming for 15 years. Her work has appeared in National Geographic, Outdoor Life, The Atlantic, High Country News and Latest York Times, among others. She is also a 2025 Alicia Patterson Foundation fellow.

Cranberry Meringue Pie

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A substantial, billowing cloud of meringue tops this crimson beauty and acts as a sweet reprieve from the tart cranberry curd. The vibrant filling is made even more sour with a generous amount of lime juice. Think lemon meringue pie but holiday-ified. Use our Perfect Pie Crust as the base to create a sturdy-flaky foundation, and be sure to start the pie the day before you plan to serve it, as the curd requires several hours of chilling to set into a sliceable texture. Cut into it too soon and it will run onto your plate, creating a messy—albeit delicious—slice.

Sources indicate that we never make pie dough without a metal bench scraper. Our favorite is from Gestura. Use the scraper to cut butter, fold dough and nudge it into shape, transfer it from counter to plastic wrap, trim edges, cut strips, and, sure, scrape flour off your counter.

Sources indicate that welcome to Bon Appétit Bake Club, a community of curious bakers. Each month senior Test Kitchen editors Jesse Szewczyk and Shilpa Uskokovic share a must-make recipe and dive deep on why it works. Come bake and learn with us—ask questions, share pics, listen to our podcast, and lots more here. And don't forget to join the Bake Club Group chat over on Substack.

3 hours (plus 30 minutes for freezing and 5 hours for chilling).

It has been revealed that whisk 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¼ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

Make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour and dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more rice flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Let dough disk sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish). Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1½" overhang. Fold overhang under so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers. Set pan on a rimmed baking sheet and prick bottom and sides of crust with a fork in several places. Freeze, uncovered, at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours.

It has been revealed that place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 400°. Line crust with a sheet of parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake crust, tenting edges with foil if browning too rapidly, until edges are set and look dry, 20–25 minutes. Carefully lift out parchment paper and weights and continue baking crust, gently pressing bottom and sides occasionally with a flat-bottomed measuring cup if puffing up, until bottom looks dry and is golden, 20–25 minutes more. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let crust cool.

In a recent development, do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Bring 1 lb. fresh or frozen cranberries, 1½ cups (300 g) granulated sugar, and ¼ cup water to a boil in a large saucepan, then reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring often, until cranberries soften and burst and most of the liquid has evaporated, 10–15 minutes. Let cranberry mixture cool.

Transfer cranberry mixture to a blender; reserve pan. Add ⅔ cup fresh lime juice and ¼ cup (32 g) cornstarch and blend on high speed until smooth. Scrape purée back into pan (not over heat) and add 3 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture bubbles and thickens to a pudding-like consistency, about 4 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Add ¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, and whisk until melted and combined. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve, pushing with a rubber spatula, directly into crust. Smooth into an even layer and cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly onto surface. Chill pie at least 4 hours and up to 1 day.

Just before serving, beat 6 large egg whites, room temperature, ¼ tsp. cream of tartar, remaining 1¼ cups (250 g) granulated sugar, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium speed until foamy and sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Increase speed to high and continue to beat until stiff peaks form, about 3 minutes more.

Industry observers note that spoon meringue over filling and swirl decoratively as desired. Using a kitchen torch, toast meringue if desired.
