  • Industry observers note that almost all of the major events that changed the trajectory of life on Earth had impossibly tiny beginnings, and the rise of plant life is no exception.
  • Despite the vast evolutionary gulf between them (the two lineages diverged in the middle of the Proterozoic Eon), a new study published in the journal Nature Communications suggests that the cells derived from red algae and mammals still have the capacity to acquire genetic material through a process known as “horizontal gene transfer.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Industry observers note that almost all of the major events that changed the trajectory of life on Earth had impossibly tiny beginnings, and the rise of plant life is no exception. Some 1.5 billion years ago, a eukaryotic cell engulfed a cyanobacterium, which eventually evolved into the chloroplast, the specialized organelle that drives photosynthesis in algae and plants. Other eukaryotic cells, of course, took a very different path, giving rise to all animals and, ultimately, the mammalian cells that make up you and me.

Despite the vast evolutionary gulf between them (the two lineages diverged in the middle of the Proterozoic Eon), a new study published in the journal Nature Communications suggests that the cells derived from red algae and mammals still have the capacity to acquire genetic material through a process known as “horizontal gene transfer.”.

Obviously, most gene transfers in nature move from parents to offspring (fittingly named “vertical gene transfer”), but sometimes cells will acquire traits from other individuals, strains, or even entire species. This is seen most commonly in bacteria that share antibiotic resistance genes, or ARGs, creating troublesome antimicrobial-resistant (or drug-resistant) superbugs in the process. However, other fascinating examples exist, including a parasitic worm that can control its host by swapping genes. In their new study, a team of scientists led by researchers at the University of Tokyo explored whether a similar process could take place between cells separated by more than a billion years of evolution, resulting in what the researchers call “planimal” cells.

Industry observers note that “We wanted to understand whether entire chromosomes could cross the enormous evolutionary divide between algae and animals and whether animal cells could stably maintain and pass on such foreign genetic material to their daughter cells,” University of Tokyo biologist Sachihiro Matsunaga, senior author of the study, remarked in a press statement. “These questions are fundamental to understanding how genetic material can move across species boundaries and contribute to evolution.”.

To investigate this possibility, the authors relied on cells derived from the red alga Cyanidioschyzon merolae, along with mammal cells originating from a hamster. Mirroring the primordial event that gave rise to plant life, the researchers allowed the mammalian cell to engulf the alga, after which—surprisingly—cell fusion produced stable hybrid cells. Armed with advanced imaging and genome sequencing, Matsunaga and his team could track how well host mammalian cells retained this algal DNA over subsequent generations. They found that 16.3 million algal base pairs and intact chromosome sequences from all 20 algal chromosomes were retained, and the algal DNA remained detectable through 155 cell generations.

According to recent reports, “Plants and animals cannot reproduce with each other, so their chromosomes are never combined through mating. Yet, we have succeeded in creating hybrid chromosomes containing genetic material from both an alga and a mammal,” Matsunaga mentioned. “This demonstrates that even the vast evolutionary divide between plants and animals can be crossed at the level of chromosomes, without reproduction.”.

The key to the planimal cells’ survival was the epigenetic “gatekeeping” ability of the host cell to essentially silence incorporated foreign DNA. The authors estimate that roughly 96 percent of the algal protein-coding genes were basically offline, but it’s possible that future studies could detect how to flip this gene switch to “on.”.

“Our ultimate goal is to activate these biological pathways and give animal cells some of the unique abilities of plants and algae,” Matsunaga added. “Imagine animal cells that could sustain photosynthesis for long periods, producing oxygen while using carbon dioxide to make useful organic compounds.”.

Darren lives in Portland, has a cat, and writes/edits about sci-fi and how our world works. You can find his previous stuff at Gizmodo and Paste if you look hard enough.

#66082. How to Blind-Bake Pie Crust—and When You Need To

How to Blind-Bake Pie Crust—and When You Need To

📅 16 May 2016 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1443 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the road to pie perfection is paved in pitfalls.
  • Industry observers note that but getting the crust to the right color depends on what you’re planning to fill it with.
  • Blind baking is especially useful when the filling needs less time in the oven than the crust does.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the road to pie perfection is paved in pitfalls. I’ve fallen into plenty of them throughout my baking career. The infamous “soggy bottom” is among the most common, but it’s easy to avoid. Blind baking—baking the crust before adding the filling—helps prevent an underbaked crust by giving the pastry a head start in the oven or cooking it completely before the filling goes in.

Industry observers note that but getting the crust to the right color depends on what you’re planning to fill it with. A pale, partially baked shell might be perfect for one pie, while another needs a deep golden brown crust before you add even a spoonful of filling. Here’s how to know when enough color is enough.

Blind baking is especially useful when the filling needs less time in the oven than the crust does. For custard pies, like pumpkin pie, partially baking the shell gives the pastry a head start so it doesn’t end up uncooked beneath a set filling. For pies with no-bake fillings, such as chocolate pudding pie or cranberry curd pie, the crust needs to be fully baked before it’s filled.

Most traditional fruit pies don’t need blind baking. Their fillings and crusts spend enough time in the oven together for the pastry to cook through. There are exceptions, particularly single-crust fruit pies topped with a crumble. Our Peach-Blueberry Pie, for example, starts with a thoroughly blind-baked shell before the filling goes in. Follow your recipe’s instructions rather than assuming every fruit pie needs the same treatment.

Start with a good pie dough. Roll it out, fit it into the pie plate, and crimp the edge. Chill the shaped shell for at least 15 minutes before baking; cold dough holds its shape better in the oven, reducing the risk of shrinking or slumping.

Next, line the shell with parchment paper and fill it with pie weights. Crumpling the parchment first, then unfolding it, helps it conform to the shell. The weights hold the dough against the pan while it bakes, preventing the bottom from puffing up and the sides from collapsing.

You can buy ceramic pie weights or use dried beans, rice, or stainless-steel ball bearings. I’m partial to the ball bearings: They’re small enough to settle into the corners of the pie plate and heavy enough to hold the dough firmly in place.

In a recent development, not everyone in the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen agrees. Editors Jesse Szewczyk and Rebecca Firkser prefer lighter alternatives. In their experience, heavy metal weights can compress the dough, limiting the expansion of the buttery layers that make pie crust flaky. Jesse uses dried beans or rice; Rebecca prefers dried chickpeas or even granulated sugar, a technique popularized by baking expert Stella Parks.

All of these options can work. Whichever you choose, fill the parchment-lined shell generously, supporting the sides all the way to the rim. Leave the weights in place until the crust looks dry and set and the parchment releases easily; removing them too soon can cause the sides to slump.

Our Cranberry Meringue Pie has a fully blind-baked pie crust.

Sources indicate that this method uses our Perfect Pie Crust dough and makes one 9"-diameter pie shell. It produces an evenly golden crust; if your pie calls for a paler or more deeply browned shell, follow its specific baking instructions and use the visual guide below.

Sources indicate that some pie recipes call for docking (pricking the bottom and sides of the dough with a fork) before baking. This allows steam to escape and helps prevent uneven puffing, but doesn’t replace the support of pie weights. Follow your recipe’s instructions; docking isn’t necessary for every blind-baked crust.

In a recent development, do Ahead: A fully blind-baked crust can be made up to 2 days ahead. Let cool completely, wrap well, and store at room temperature until ready to fill.

The short answer: It depends on what you’re putting inside. Some pies need only a partially baked crust, while others call for a shell that’s deeply golden brown.

Industry observers note that oven temperatures vary, different pie plates conduct heat differently, and the filling determines how much additional baking the crust will get. Use the recipe’s timing as a guide, but watch the color and texture of the pastry. Here’s what to look for.

According to recent reports, fruit pies need a pale base because they bake a looong time. Or at least, that’s often the thinking. If you’re making a single-crust variety topped with a crumble, such as our Blueberry Crumble Pie, and the recipe calls for blind-baking, you might want to start with an anemic crust. It’ll have plenty of time to brown as the juices thicken.

In a recent development, A pale, partially baked crust should look set rather than raw. The bottom should look set and opaque with some light golden patches, while the crimped edge may already be noticeably browned. The crust will continue to develop color once the filling goes in.

Don’t assume fruit pies always need a pale shell. Our Peach-Blueberry Pie, for example, calls for a well-browned crust before the fruit and crumble go in. And many double-crust fruit pies don’t need blind baking at all.

A lightly baked shell can also be appropriate for custards that have a substantial bake ahead. BA’s Best Pumpkin Pie starts with a partially baked crust before the custard goes in for at least another hour.

The goal is to give the crust enough of a head start without taking it so far that the edges burn before the filling finishes cooking.

Custard pies, such as chess and our Lemon Buttermilk Pie, often have shorter bake times than fruit pies, so the crust needs a solid golden base layer to develop enough color by the time the filling sets.

Here, you’re looking for more than a crust that’s simply dry and set. The bottom should be evenly golden with no pale, translucent patches, and the sides should have taken on some color too. The rim will generally be a little darker than the bottom, but the whole shell should look well on its way to being fully baked.

Our Perfect Pie Crust recipe produces this kind of shell. It calls for baking the weighted crust until the edges are golden, then removing the weights and continuing until the bottom and sides are evenly browned.

It has been revealed that and some pies need an even more substantial head start. Our Bourbon-Date Pecan Pie takes the crust to a dry golden finish before adding a filling that bakes for another 45–55 minutes.

According to recent reports, the point isn’t that every custard pie needs the same color. It’s that the crust should be baked far enough that it won’t be left pale and doughy by the time the filling is done.

According to recent reports, bake the crust to a dark golden brown if you’re adding a no-bake filling, like a pudding or curd. You’re going for a toasty, burnished color, so don’t be gun-shy.

Because the filling won’t return to the oven, this is the crust’s one chance to bake all the way through. You want deep color across the entire bottom and up the sides—not just a dark rim surrounding a pale center. The pastry should look dry, crisp, and well browned, without any doughy or translucent spots.

It has been revealed that after removing the pie weights, continue baking until the shell is fully browned, checking frequently toward the end. Depending on the dough and oven temperature, that might take another 15–20 minutes or longer. Don’t pull it simply because the timer has gone off.

It has been revealed that our Cranberry Meringue Pie uses this approach: The crust is baked until golden and dry before the cranberry curd filling goes in. A fully baked shell develops a richer, toastier flavor and is better equipped to stand up to a moist filling.

According to recent reports, some recipes, including our pumpkin pie, call for brushing a thin layer of beaten egg onto the partially baked shell and returning it to the oven briefly to set. This, ostensibly, creates a barrier between the pastry and the filling, but not all bakers believe the hype.

While it can be a useful extra precaution, it is by no means a universal requirement. If your recipe doesn’t call for it, there’s no need to add another step.

They’ll be here whenever you need them.

Editor’s note: This story was originally published in May 2016 and has been updated with additional reporting and expanded instructions by Phoebe Fry.

Wendy’s Brought Back A Beloved Piece Of Its Past—Plus Two New Holiday Frostys

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The fast food chain just launched a limited-time Holiday Box complete with retro packaging, collectible knit hats, and a choice of some familiar menu favorites.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wendy’s is getting nostalgic this holiday season, and as someone who grew up eating in one of the chain’s iconic glass sunrooms, I’m particularly excited about this one.

The fast food chain just launched a limited-time Holiday Box complete with retro packaging, collectible knit hats, and a choice of some familiar menu favorites. And of course, two fresh peppermint-inspired Frosty desserts.

Obviously, I had to try everything for myself.

Available beginning November 16 at participating Wendy’s locations nationwide, the Holiday Box starts at $11.99 and includes your choice of a Dave’s Double or 10-piece crispy or spicy chicken nuggets, small fries, a small soft drink, and one collectible knit hat.

The packaging is designed to resemble Wendy’s old-school Solarium restaurants, complete with the recognizable glass-walled dining area that became a staple of the chain beginning in the 1980s.

And I have to admit, this one hit me right in the childhood memories.

Industry observers note that growing up, I remember going to Wendy’s with my mom and sitting in that yellow, glass-enclosed sunroom. Seeing the design recreated as a miniature holiday box immediately brought me back to those visits.

Each Holiday Box includes one of four collectible knit hats featuring a retro Wendy’s design: Frosty, Biggie, the classic Wendy’s logo, or the famous “Where’s the Beef?” slogan.

The hats come in sealed mystery bags, meaning you won’t know which one you’re getting until you open it.

Thankfully, I ended up with the blue Frosty beanie, which was exactly the design I was hoping for.

Had I opened the bag to find a hat with “Biggie” written across my forehead, though, I think we would’ve had a problem.

The Holiday Box is available for a limited time while supplies last, and customers can’t select which hat they receive.

Alongside the Holiday Box, Wendy’s is introducing two limited-time desserts: the Peppermint Frosty Swirl and Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion.

Both are available with either a vanilla or chocolate Frosty base, so I decided to try one of each.

This was easily my favorite of the two.

The Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion combines Wendy’s classic Frosty with peppermint sauce and brownie pieces, creating a dessert that feels especially appropriate for the holiday season.

I went with the vanilla base, and I absolutely loved it.

According to recent reports, the peppermint flavor was strong and immediately reminded me of a candy cane or a York Peppermint Pattie. It had that recognizable minty sweetness I look for in a holiday dessert, without getting lost in the vanilla Frosty.

Industry observers note that the brownie pieces were another highlight, adding a nice texture and a layer of chocolate flavor to the mix. I particularly liked how the chocolate complemented the peppermint rather than competing with it.

Industry observers note that for me, this is exactly what a seasonal Frosty should taste like. It’s festive, flavorful, and different enough from the regular menu to make it worth trying.

For my second dessert, I went with the chocolate Peppermint Frosty Swirl, which combines Wendy’s classic Chocolate Frosty with peppermint sauce.

My biggest piece of advice is to give this one a good stir before digging in.

When I first tried it, most of the peppermint syrup was concentrated toward the top of the dessert. Mixing everything together helped distribute the flavor more evenly throughout the Frosty.

Once I did that, I really enjoyed it.

The combination of chocolate and peppermint works well, although I didn’t find the mint flavor nearly as strong as it was in the vanilla Brownie Frosty Fusion.

Sources indicate that still, I’m happy to report that Wendy’s peppermint sauce works with both Frosty flavors. If you prefer a more straightforward chocolate-mint combination without brownie pieces, this is a solid option.

Personally, though, I’d go back for the Fusion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Forget the traditional opening-night fanfare. If love is a many-splendored thing, apparently it’s also bright pink and best enjoyed with a ’90s dance anthem blasting in the background.

William Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing arrived at the Winter Garden Theatre on Thursday with an explosion of fuchsia confetti, a giant inflatable heart, and seriously impressive dance moves from Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell. Shakespeare, it seemed, was ready to party.

According to recent reports, following its successful run in London’s West End, the production crossed the Atlantic with Hiddleston and Atwell reprising their roles as Benedick and Beatrice, two sharp-witted characters who trade barbs before falling in love. At the show’s helm is acclaimed British director Jamie Lloyd, known for his bold, contemporary reimaginings of classic plays and musicals. With Much Ado About Nothing, he’s given Shakespeare’s romantic comedy a gloriously over-the-top makeover.

It has been revealed that the party started long before the curtain rose. From the moment guests stepped into the Winter Garden, ushers danced down the aisles, greeting theatergoers as though they were arriving at the hottest club. Cynthia Nixon, Rachel Zegler, Bryan Cranston, Claire Danes, Angela Bassett, Bob Odenkirk, Hugh Dancy, and Busy Philipps were among the familiar faces in the crowd, which had enough star power to rival the theatrical fireworks unfolding onstage.

Industry observers note that as Benedick and Beatrice, Hiddleston, best known to many as Marvel’s Loki, and Atwell, who played Agent Peggy Carter in the MCU, made an irresistibly mischievous pairing—dancing, singing, and flirting with infectious enthusiasm. Their characters’ courtship is one of literature’s great enemies-to-lovers stories, and the pair brought every barb, raised eyebrow, and moment of romantic tension brilliantly to life.

“I can’t do much, but I can lunge,” Hiddleston modestly told Vogue of his dancing before curtain. “The dancing is sufficiently irreverent and giddy and silly and free as this play, and I’m having the best time.”.

It has been revealed that dressed in a Ralph Lauren tuxedo, he described his opening-night feelings as “joyous and joyful,” declaring his love for the play, his fellow cast members, and the production. It was during his previous collaboration with Lloyd that the seeds for this one were planted. “When I was last on Broadway, for the production of Betrayal, Jamie said to me on the last night, ‘What are we doing next?’ I thought he was joking and I said, ‘Much Ado About Nothing,’ and here we are!”.

In a recent development, for Atwell, the evening marked a major milestone in her nearly 25-year acting career: she was making her Broadway debut. Clad in a chic Erdem ensemble, she reflected on the significance of the occasion shortly before taking the stage. “It’s really remarkable. It’s not lost on me how special this moment is,” she said. “Rather than being overwhelmed by it, I really want to take it in and to cherish it.” She described herself as staying “calm amongst the excitable storm of it all.”.

Atwell was also having a blast with the production’s choreography, giving audiences a chance to see a different side of her. “I don’t have any formal dance training apart from going to the clubs,” she stated, laughing. “I get to have a party every night onstage, and make moves I didn’t know I had. So it’s really fun.” The dancing came with a few occupational hazards, however, including sore knees and the occasional spill. “I’ve already slipped on my ass twice, and that felt like an initiation,” she shared. Rather than rattling her, the falls actually made her more confident: “I can survive this. I can get up and carry on.”.

In a recent development, for all the fuchsia and dance-floor theatrics, the production left the Bard’s text alone. “I’ve always believed that Shakespeare should be spoken as if it was written right now or yesterday,” Hiddleston stated. “There’s no word of this play that isn’t the 400-year-old text by Shakespeare. We have dressed it in the energy of dancing and music and levity, but the play itself is the play that it always was.”.

He went on: “Come because it will speak to your heart. This play is funny. It’s been funny for 400 years. We’ll make it easy for you.”.

Industry observers note that dressed in a custom pink Levi’s suit, Lloyd told Vogue that the show’s abundance of confetti—which erupts during a jubilant party scene, blanketing the stage and eventually spilling into the audience—is about more than just spectacle. “It’s certainly a lot and it’s used in a really exciting way, to show the celebration of love and joy—and that’s what the play is all about. It feels like we really need that right now.”.

According to recent reports, the party continued well after the curtain came down. Following a standing ovation, the cast and guests headed to Tavern on the Green for the after-party, where lavish food stations served tacos, pasta, salmon, and steak skewers, while the Prosecco flowed—and, yes, people hit the dance floor.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I tried hash browns from five different fast food chains to see which one serves up the best during the morning rush.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

People across the country take breakfast very seriously—after all, many believe it's the most notable meal of the day. When you're rushing to work, grabbing something on the go is often the easiest option. And nothing screams breakfast quite like a side of hash browns. When a diner isn't in the cards, a fast food chain can be just the ticket.

I tried hash browns from five different fast food chains to see which one serves up the best during the morning rush. Of the chains I tried, only Dunkin' serves hash browns all day. Everywhere else, you'll need to order during breakfast hours, which vary by location.

According to recent reports, this proved to be one of the tougher taste tests I've conducted during my time at Delish. There were truly no terrible options, and some of the differences were pretty small. Here's how they stacked up.

Burger King's hash browns come in a handy carton filled with plenty of small, round crisps. They have a crunchy exterior and, honestly, are perfectly adequate. They're just up against some tough contenders. Of all the spuds I tried, these were the least memorable and had the least flavor, though nothing about them was off-putting.

Sources indicate that taco Bell served the most substantial hash brown on this list—it was quite hefty. The exterior had a nice crispiness, but compared to its competitors, the inside was much mushier, and the whole thing was noticeably greasier. It's not something I could eat a lot of.

According to recent reports, dunkin's hash browns, which are served all day (!), were a bit more divisive in the Delish office. Some people stood ten toes down for the zesty onion flavor, while others (myself included) found it more reminiscent of leftover grease on a stove. That said, the texture was great, and whether you love them or hate them, these had the boldest flavor and stood out from the rest of the pack.

In a recent development, like Taco Bell, McDonald's offers a larger hash brown patty than the others on this list. The chain totally nails the crispy outer edges and boasts great potato flavor. You can really tell this is McDonald's because the taste is so similar to the chain's iconic fries. If you like those, you'll love its hash browns. However, because of the patty's size, the middle lost some of the structure and crispiness I was looking for.

It has been revealed that in a surprise win, Chick-fil-A's hash browns came out on top. The bite-sized pieces are easy to grab on the go, and their small size gives each one the perfect mix of a crispy exterior and soft interior. The flavor is spot-on, with savory onion and pepper notes. Best of all, they weren't overly greasy.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The redistricting fights that underscored this year’s battle for the House could continue into the 2028 election cycle, although lessons from last Tuesday will likely shape those efforts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, here at the Capitol in January, wants to see his state's congressional map redrawn. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The redistricting fights that underscored this year’s battle for the House could continue into the 2028 election cycle, although lessons from last Tuesday will likely shape those efforts.

According to recent reports, house Republicans had hoped that new congressional maps in seven states would help them limit losses in the face of an unfavorable political environment. But nearly a week after the election, the GOP appeared on track to flip just three redrawn seats while losing a host of seats in Texas, Florida, North Carolina, Ohio and Alabama that were reconfigured in their favor.

“The question is whether the results have let some air out of the [redistricting] balloon or not,” mentioned Erik Nisbet, a professor at Northwestern University’s School of Communication.

It has been revealed that republicans may question the utility of redrawing more state maps in the 2028 cycle, while Democrats will need to weigh how to spend their political capital. But the fresh lines approved over the past year could still prove more favorable for Republicans in future elections.

“This was a wave election, and there’s no guarantee that the Democratic generic ballot would be D+13 — which is the reason why redistricting didn’t work for Republicans — in the next cycle,” Nisbet added.

Recent findings suggest that new maps appear possible, if not likely, in at least a few states. Maryland voters last week approved an amendment that would clear the way for new boundaries ahead of the 2028 elections. Democratic Gov. Wes Moore, who easily won a second term last week, remarked he hopes to see a new map, citing the threat of President Donald Trump continuing to push for friendlier lines in GOP-led states. Maryland Democrats could draw a map that would favor them in all eight of the state’s House seats, including the Eastern Shore district of Rep. Andy Harris, the state’s lone Republican in Congress.

Advocates for a new map in Wisconsin got a boost last week when Democrats flipped both the state House and state Senate, setting up a Democratic trifecta. Gov.-elect David Crowley said he would sign a bill redrawing the state’s congressional map if legislators sent one to his desk.

According to recent reports, republicans in recent years have had a lopsided edge in the congressional delegation for Wisconsin, a perennial battleground state. But Democrats flipped two House seats last week, with Rebecca Cooke and Mitchell Berman unseating GOP Reps. Derrick Van Orden and Bryan Steil, respectively, bringing the state delegation to an even 4-4.

Democrats could also look to redraw the lines in New York and Virginia. Earlier this year, voters in the commonwealth approved a new map that would have given Democrats up to four pickup opportunities, but the Virginia Supreme Court later struck it down on procedural grounds. Even without the new map, Democrats flipped two House seats in Virginia last week and came within 2 points of flipping a third.

Democrats in Fresh York, meanwhile, took initial steps toward mid-decade redistricting earlier this year, but 2028 is the earliest they could hold elections under a new map.

On the Republican side, several states have been mentioned as candidates for upcoming maps in 2028.

Officials in GOP-led Mississippi have held hearings this year on redistricting, which could target Democratic Rep. Bennie Thompson. Republicans are also aiming to redraw the state’s legislative lines ahead of next year’s off-year elections.

It’s not clear whether states that were unsuccessful in redrawing their district lines for 2026 will try again when their legislatures convene next year. Republicans in both South Carolina and Indiana fell short in their push to pass new maps and could decide to revisit the glitch. But Democrats flipped a House seat in each state last week, and some Republican incumbents won reelection by narrower margins than usual. Still, Republicans maintained their legislative majorities in both states, though Democrats broke their supermajorities in the South Carolina and Indiana state houses.

An analysis by DecisionDeskHQ offers a potential warning sign for Republicans in the Palmetto and Hoosier states: Under the GOP-drawn maps that were not adopted for 2026, Democrats could have flipped even more seats last week.

Redistricting appears off the table in a handful of states where new maps for 2028 had once been considered possible.

Georgia’s outgoing Republican governor, Brian Kemp, said last week that he would not call a special session to address redistricting before the end of the year, after Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected to succeed him.

There were no House flips in the Peach State in the midterm elections, though several Republicans won by closer-than-anticipated margins.

In Upcoming Jersey, Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill told the New Jersey Globe that she also did not “see a path forward for redistricting right now.”.

Democrats flipped two House seats in the Garden State last week. Navy veteran Rebecca Bennett defeated Republican Rep. Thomas H. Kean Jr., while Cape May Mayor Zack Mullock scored a surprise win over GOP Rep. Jeff Van Drew.

With their fresh majorities in Washington, Democrats could propose legislation to ban partisan gerrymandering.

That’s something John Bisognano, the president of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, anticipates happening, but he stated Democrat-led states should be prepared to respond to latest maps drawn in Republican-controlled ones.

“If they are going to continue to take those actions, Democrats in states across the country need to be prepared to respond, and we, of course, now have significantly more opportunities than we did before Tuesday to respond to those states,” he said.

It has been revealed that cut this festive galette into little squares for a hearty appetizer, or serve sizeable wedges as a vegetarian main or standout side. It’s worth seeking out savoy cabbage, the ruffly sort that looks like lace. Ordinary green cabbage, which has a higher moisture content and flatter texture, doesn’t work here (we tried).

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Industry observers note that whisk 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ¼ tsp. baking powder, and 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour in a large bowl. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub in with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea size). Make a well in the center and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute. Knead dough in bowl just to bring together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn dough out onto a lightly dusted surface and sprinkle with all-purpose flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting dough with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

It has been revealed that do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

It has been revealed that when dough is almost done chilling, cut 1 medium head of savoy cabbage (1¾–2¼ lb.) in half and cut out triangular core at bottom; discard. Separate leaves and tear into pieces about the size of your palm. Transfer about half to a large bowl and set aside.

Melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 medium white or yellow onion, thinly sliced, and season generously with kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to turn translucent, about 5 minutes. Add remaining 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter and ¾ tsp. cumin seeds (if using) and cook until butter is melted. Add remaining cabbage leaves and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent and lightly browned and cabbage is wilted, 18–22 minutes. Transfer to a large plate or a small baking sheet; chill in fridge or freezer until cool.

Sources indicate that place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 400°. Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ⅓ cup heavy cream, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a measuring glass to combine. Pour cream mixture over reserved raw cabbage leaves and toss with your hands to coat. Add 5 oz. Gruyère or sharp cheddar, coarsely grated, and toss again to combine.

It has been revealed that unwrap dough and roll out on a lightly floured sheet of parchment paper to a 13–14" round (some dough will extend beyond the parchment). Transfer on parchment paper to a baking sheet.

Sources indicate that spread cooked cabbage mixture over dough, leaving about a 1½" border around edges. Fold dough up and over filling, folding and tucking as needed to make a rustic border. Pile raw cabbage mixture on top of cooked cabbage mixture to make a dramatic heap. (It will look ridiculously high at first but will cook down when it bakes.).

It has been revealed that bake galette 25 minutes. Rotate baking sheet front to back, reduce heat to 375°, and bake until cabbage and crust are deep golden brown, 25–35 minutes. (If cabbage seems to be browning too much, reduce heat to 350° toward the end.) Let galette cool on baking sheet at least 1 hour and up to 4 hours before serving.

It has been revealed that do Ahead: Sautéed cabbage can be made 1 day ahead. Transfer to an airtight container and chill. Tightly wrap undressed raw cabbage in plastic and chill.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Brown sugar and a spoonful of dark molasses add depth to the filling, while toasting the pecans before incorporating them makes their flavor stand out and their texture more robust.
  • Industry observers note that when the pie comes out of the oven, the edges should be set and slightly puffed, but the center should still wobble like Jell-O.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, our classic pecan pie recipe has no chocolate chips, no booze, and no hard-to-find ingredients. Instead of focusing on embellishments, we focused on what matters most: the deep flavor of toasted pecans, a caramelly custard, and a buttery, flaky pie crust.

Brown sugar and a spoonful of dark molasses add depth to the filling, while toasting the pecans before incorporating them makes their flavor stand out and their texture more robust. Blind baking the crust—baking it before adding the filling—helps keep the bottom crisp beneath the gooey custard.

Industry observers note that when the pie comes out of the oven, the edges should be set and slightly puffed, but the center should still wobble like Jell-O. It will continue to set as it cools, so resist slicing too soon. Serve it all on its own, or gild it with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

Can I make this pecan pie without corn syrup?

Yes. Corn syrup gives this classic pie its perfectly gooey texture, but there are alternatives. Brown rice syrup will add a toasty flavor and can be used in equal parts. Golden syrup, honey, and maple syrup are all too sweet and will change the pie’s flavor and texture.

For a pie developed without any syrup, try our Bourbon-Date Pecan Pie.

Can I use chopped pecans instead of halves?

Yes. We love the crunch you get from pecan halves, but if you’re a chopped pecan person, use about 225 g in place of the 2 cups of halves. Watch closely when toasting; chopped pecans will need less time in the oven.

Can I make pecan pie ahead of time?

In a recent development, yes—bake the pie a day ahead and refrigerate it. Let it cool on a rack for up to 2 hours, then transfer it to the refrigerator to finish cooling before covering. To get a head start on the pastry, refrigerate the dough for up to 3 days or freeze it for up to 2 months.

Pulse 1 Tbsp. sugar, 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 2 cups all-purpose flour in a food processor until combined. Add 5 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 3 Tbsp. chilled lard or vegetable shortening and pulse until mixture resembles coarse meal with a few pieces of butter and lard visible, about fifteen 1-second pulses. With motor running, drizzle in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar and 5½ Tbsp. ice water and pulse until dough is still crumbly but just holds together when squeezed (add 1 tsp. water at a time if necessary, but be careful not to overwork dough).

Turn out dough onto a work surface. Knead 1–2 times, pressing just to incorporate any shaggy pieces. Flatten into a 6"-wide disk. Wrap with plastic wrap and chill at least 1 hour.

According to recent reports, preheat oven to 425°. Roll out dough on a lightly floured work surface to a 14" round. Transfer to a 9" pie pan. Pick up edges and allow dough to slump down into dish, letting excess dough hang over dish. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Fold overhang under; pinch and crimp. Chill 30 minutes.

Sources indicate that line dough with parchment paper or foil, leaving some overhang. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until crust is dry around the edges and just beginning to lightly brown, 25–35 minutes. Carefully remove parchment and weights and reduce oven temperature to 350°. Bake until crust is set and beginning to brown in the center, 10–15 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool.

Do Ahead: Dough can be made 3 days ahead; keep chilled, or freeze up to 2 months. Crust can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and store at room temperature.

In a recent development, preheat oven to 350°. Toast 2 cups (225 g) pecan halves on a rimmed baking sheet until browned and fragrant, 8–10 minutes. Let cool.

Reduce oven temperature to 325°. Whisk 4 large eggs, room temperature, beaten to blend, 1 cup light corn syrup, ⅔ cup (packed; 134 g) light brown sugar, 1 Tbsp. robust-flavored (dark) molasses, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl until smooth. Slowly whisk in 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, until combined. Fold in pecans and pour into cooled crust.

Recent findings suggest that bake pie until edges are set and slightly puffed but center is recessed and wobbles like Jell-O, 55–70 minutes (it will continue to set after baking). Transfer to a wire rack and let cool at least 3 hours before slicing. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

Industry observers note that do Ahead: Pie can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and chill. Serve warm or at room temperature.

The Unstoppable Cecilia Vicuña

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a perfect fall day, bright and brisk, when I meet the Chilean artist and poet Cecilia Vicuña at her studio in Tribeca, just a few blocks away from the loft she’s lived in for the last 46 years.
  • As someone so closely tethered to the natural world, Vicuña wishes we could go outside and enjoy it.
  • Vicuña, 78, is a seeker of many things: truth, justice, beauty, connection with people and the earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a perfect fall day, bright and brisk, when I meet the Chilean artist and poet Cecilia Vicuña at her studio in Tribeca, just a few blocks away from the loft she’s lived in for the last 46 years.

As someone so closely tethered to the natural world, Vicuña wishes we could go outside and enjoy it. We can, I offer—there’s no reason to stay cooped up inside for our entire conversation. Grinning, she agrees to show me her studio first. “And then we seek the sun.”.

Vicuña, 78, is a seeker of many things: truth, justice, beauty, connection with people and the earth. For more than five decades she has brought attention to under-recognized voices through her sculptures, paintings, poems, videos, sound installations, and performances. For many of those years she worked in relative obscurity, known in certain avant-garde and activist circles in Fresh York and South America, but unacknowledged by the establishment. But the global art world woke up to her brilliance about a decade ago, especially when her quipus—hanging sculptures made from wool that nod to the ancient Andean knot systems—attracted attention at Documenta 14 in Germany and Greece.

“Everything else disappeared next to it,” says gallerist Rachel Lehmann of the one she saw in Athens. Needing to know more about the artist of this magnificent work, she paid Vicuña a visit back in New York, and Lehmann Maupin began representing her in 2018. Since then it’s been a swift rise. In 2022, Vicuña was awarded the Venice Biennale’s Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement, one of the most prestigious prizes in contemporary art.

Vicuña’s studio, a “little hideout,” she calls it, is filled with sacred begonias, money trees, and aloe plants. During my visit she’s preparing for two new exhibitions, one on each coast of the US. On November 15, the Museum of Contemporary Art in Los Angeles unveiled “The Dream of Water: Quipu of Encounters Maricunga,” a multipart commission tied to the inaugural Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize. And on November 19, Lehmann Maupin opened a show in New York City of several new Vicuña paintings and a video alongside the work of Surrealist painter Leonora Carrington, the first time their artwork will be in direct dialogue. (All this on the heels of Vicuña’s first major exhibition in the UK, presently on view at Whitechapel Gallery in London after appearing in Dublin, and a show in MASS MoCA that opened in the spring.).

Sources indicate that the quipus are Vicuña’s best-known works. While a quipu can take physical form, often in vibrant strands of wool with knots intuitively tied at various intervals that hang from the ceiling and pool at the floor, its spirit extends far beyond sculpture. “From the Western perspective, quipu is an object that you find on an archeological mission. But from my perspective, it’s a way of being,” she says. “It’s a way of connecting yourself to other people, to the land, to the future. The quipu begins when I start thinking about it.”.

There’s one thing in particular she’s been thinking about for the MoCA exhibition, which underpins its many components: the ecological crisis unfolding in the Maricunga salt flats in Chile’s Atacama Desert, brought on by lithium mining. Lithium is often referred to as white gold for its use in the batteries that power the green energy revolution. But the extraction methods are a direct threat to the already scarce water supply of the Indigenous Colla people, as well as the ancient microorganisms and parinas, or flamingos, that call the region home.

It has been revealed that protection of Indigenous culture has long been at the core of Vicuña’s practice. As a young girl, decades before it was confirmed by a DNA test, Vicuña knew she had American Indian blood, and indeed her mother’s side traces back to the Diaguita people. The fight against colonialism, patriarchy, environmental collapse—it’s all personal to her.

It has been revealed that “Cecilia was very clear about what she wanted to do” with the project, says José Luis Blondet, a senior curator at MoCA who organized the show with curatorial assistant Ariana Rizo and environmental adviser Kelsey Shell. Vicuña made two trips to the Atacama Desert to connect with artists, scientists, Indigenous leaders, musicians, and others to perform rituals together, a collective intention-setting. “I believe we have to dream a different culture,” she says. “Dream from the Indigenous perspective is the way to create realities. So you dream with the intent that the dream will be a seed.”.

Scenes from her visits will replay at MoCA in a poetic five-channel video installation. Nearby, in the museum’s tallest gallery, hangs Parina Quipu, a 30-foot-long work of skeins of unspun wool in vibrant pinks with bits of brown and gray streaked in, mimicking the dramatic Martian landscape of the Atacama. “The beauty there is divine,” Vicuña says.

Sources indicate that the third component of the MoCA show will arrive next spring with a series of performances and rituals, a Vicuña specialty that she calls a “quipu of encounters.” For this one, she’ll gather Los Angeles water guardians and her collaborators like Cristina Dorador, an acclaimed Chilean scientist whose ongoing study of the Atacama Desert’s microbial life was crucial to Vicuña’s understanding of the crisis there. “What is happening at the Atacama Desert is happening right here, right now,” notes Blondet. “Different version, different elements, but it’s the same struggle.”.

In a recent development, in addition to her quipus, the key to understanding Vicuña’s work is arte precario, the term she invented for the poignant little configurations she started making back in the 1960s out of bits of trash. She was still living in Chile then, not yet 20 years old.

“Precario means what is fragile, what might disappear,” she tells me as we sit in her studio, her voice soft (she gets much louder when she laughs, which is often). “But it disappears to regenerate life, to regenerate potentials. To stay in the potential—that’s what precario means.”.

According to recent reports, she has experienced plenty of precariousness herself. In 1972 she traveled to London to attend the Slade School of Fine Art on a scholarship. The following year a military coup overthrew the democratically elected Chilean president, Salvador Allende, and a brutal dictatorship under Augusto Pinochet began. People she knew back home were tortured, disappeared. Her father lost his job managing public pensions. It wasn’t safe to return, so she sought asylum in England, and in London she cofounded an organization called Artists for Democracy in solidarity with liberation struggles in Chile and around the world.

Precarios may represent instability, but they are also doused in hope. “When you’re aware of your death and your fragility, it’s like you acquire a different kind of power,” Vicuña says. “There’s a new freedom because you cease to be afraid. And you can be absolutely joyful, because there’s air to breathe.”.

Industry observers note that the Lehmann Maupin show this fall highlights an key kinship between Vicuña and Leonora Carrington. Vicuña stayed with Carrington in Mexico City in 1969 on her way back to Chile from Newly introduced York. Though 31 years apart in age, the two connected easily. “We had this really beautiful encounter,” she remembers. Carrington had read the young Vicuña’s poems, which had been published in a Mexican poetry magazine when she was a teenager, while Carrington was already a star in Mexico City’s avant-garde scene.

Vicuña was only there a few days, but her friend Coca Roccatagliata, also a Chilean artist, stayed with Carrington even longer and learned her techniques of translating visions into paintings—called calcomanías—which she passed along to Vicuña once back in Chile.

Recent findings suggest that “I think this was major,” indicates Lehmann. More framework than set of rules, Carrington’s tips helped Vicuña transfer the pictures in her head onto canvas. She went on to make figurative paintings in a style that mashed up Surrealism with folklore, politics, and eroticism.

Sources indicate that many of Vicuña’s early paintings were lost in the years of Chile’s dictatorship. Recently she has set about remaking them, often from memory. Her Medusa at Lehmann Maupin has two dates: 1972, for the original, and 2023, when it was re-created.

The brand-new paintings are no less affecting, and pair well with mysterious Carrington works like Eye Witness from 1987, made when she was 70. Vicuña’s Dos Trenzas demonstrates a woman with two long braids skipping toward a mountain. Cuatro Lideresas depicts four Indigenous women leaders. Vicuña had in mind the two months she spent hitchhiking through the Amazon in 1977, when the Trans-Amazonian Highway was not yet complete. “There would be highway, and then a river four times as immense. And they had no bridge, nothing. So you had to wait there until a sort of little balsa”—a raft—“would come from the other side, maybe today, maybe tomorrow.”.

As promised, we make our way out of the studio and into the autumn air. Winding through Tribeca to get to the Hudson River, which she does every day, she remarks on how much the neighborhood has changed since she moved here in 1980. It was dark, no lights, few people, rubble everywhere. She’d wriggle through a fence to get to the water’s edge back then, collecting basuritas, little trash, to make her precarios.

I ask if picking things up from the ground has ever gotten her in trouble. There was one time, around the mid-’80s, when she was weaving weeds and debris atop pools of water on the pavement. “I heard this breath behind me,” she notes. It was a police horse. “What are you doing here, young lady? This is illegal,” she remembers the officer saying. And then who indicates up but the artist Richard Tuttle, a neighbor. “He starts scolding the policeman and tells him, ‘She is a very well-known artist.’ It was completely untrue! Nobody knew me at that time.”.

Industry observers note that we arrive at one of her favorite spots at Hudson River Park, where the pier narrows to a point. Nimble as a teenager, she drops to her stomach to look out at the water from as close a vantage point as possible, and beckons me to join. “Isn’t this like being in a boat?” she asks.

She tells me about the confluence of the Hudson’s two currents. “The Native name for the river is River That Flows Both Ways,” she states. “And you can certainly see when they’re in the middle, fighting—finally, one wins.”.

“The Dream of Water: Quipu of Encounters Maricunga” is on view at MoCA Grand Avenue in Los Angeles through June 6, 2027. “Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicuña” is on view at Lehmann Maupin gallery in Upcoming York City through December 19, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the issue could occur by Wednesday.

A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Massie's resolution also charges Hegseth with disregarding protection of civilians in wartime and suppressing the free speech of a U.S. senator.

Massie confirmed his intention to file the resolution as a matter of the privileges of the House.

According to recent reports, speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., will now have to rule as to whether the resolution constitutes a proper question of the privileges of the House. There is precedent from prior instances when impeachment was found to be valid as it relates to the House’s constitutionally granted powers.

In a recent development, for those who might shudder at the thought of eating raw hardy greens like collards or kale, this vibrant side inspired by the French bistro classic leeks vinaigrette is the answer. Simmered past squeaky-raw yet well short of meltingly braised, they offer substantial bite, like al dente pasta. For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Toast ½ cup raw walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, cook 2 bunches collard greens, ribs and stems removed, leaves cut into 2" pieces, in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until just tender, 9–11 minutes. Using tongs, immediately transfer to a large bowl of ice water and let cool.

In a recent development, whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ¼ cup white wine vinegar, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, preferably country-style, ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup (packed) coarsely chopped tarragon, 2 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl to combine. Set dressing aside.

Sources indicate that transfer toasted walnuts to a small bowl and drizzle with remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with a generous pinch each of sugar and salt and toss to coat. Taste and add more sugar if needed (nuts should be more sweet than salty). Set seasoned walnuts aside.

Drain collard greens and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Transfer to bowl with reserved dressing and toss to coat evenly. Cover and chill at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours.

In a recent development, arrange greens in a shallow bowl or on a platter and spoon any dressing remaining in bowl over. Top with seasoned walnuts and tarragon leaves.

Do Ahead: Walnuts can be toasted and dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Store walnuts airtight at room temperature. Cover dressing and chill.

Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

A cordless stick vacuum has the potential to be one of the most convenient cleaning tools in your home. These lightweight machines make it easy to clean up pet hair from area rugs and hidden dust along baseboards, without having to haul out an upright vacuum or wrestling with a power cord. Most models also convert into handheld vacuums, giving you more flexibility to clean furniture, stairs, and other hard-to-reach spots.

Suction power, battery life, maneuverability, and dustbin capacities vary between models, so the right cordless stick vacuum ultimately depends on your home’s flooring, how much debris you’re dealing with, and the features that will actually make your cleaning routine easier.

We’ve rounded up the best cordless stick vacuums worth considering based on our hands-on experience, with options for everything from everyday maintenance to deeper carpet cleaning.

🔎 Looking for more ways to keep your floors and furniture clean? Check out our stories on the best robot vacuums, the best vacuums for pet hair, the best vacuums for hardwood floors, and the best handheld vacuums.

Sources indicate that I’ve spent considerable time researching, testing, and vetting all types of vacuums, so I’ve developed a pretty good understanding of what separates a genuinely useful appliance from one that is just going to take up space in your storage closet. I’ve evaluated a wide range of models, including full-size uprights, canister vacuums, robot, and handheld models vacuums, paying close attention to performance, ease of use, and features that can really make a difference in a your regular cleaning routine.

It has been revealed that when testing cordless stick vacuums, we assessed how well each model could handle common household debris, its ability to transition between carpet and hardwood floors, and how easy it was to move around furniture and into tighter spaces. We also looked at the practical considerations like battery life, suction power, dustbin capacity, weight, filtration, and included attachments.

In a recent development, beyond just how the vacuum cleans, we also considered the overall experience for an owner. Removable batteries, self-cleaning docking stations, washable filters, and easy-to-empty dustbins can also make daily vacuuming less of a drag. The below recommendations are both powerful and dependable for a wide range of cleaning needs and surface types.

The Dyson V15 Detect is the most expensive stick vacuum in our lineup, but if you can stomach the price tag, you’ll get a cordless stick vacuum that (quite literally) leaves the competition in the dust across the board. It delivers top-notch performance on floors and carpets to tackle everything from fine dust and pet dander to larger debris.

According to recent reports, its motor spins up to 125,000 rpm and it comes with two cleaning heads, including an upgraded version of the brand’s “fluffy” head that features a green laser headlight to detect fine dust. During testing, we found that being able to switch from cordless to handheld made it easier to transition from tackling small messes to deeper cleaning sessions.

The auto mode is a nice feature for conserving battery life, as this model only runs for about an hour off one charge. Another highlight is the motorized pet tool.

Full Dyson V15 Detect Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

The PowerClean FurFinder is a more affordable alternative to the PowerClean FurGuard we recommend, but that doesn’t mean you have to give up useful features.

This cordless stick vacuum is intended for use on a variety of floor types, and the flat-lay construction makes cleaning under furniture much more accessible. The vacuum also stands up on its own which leads to fewer interruptions during a cleaning session.

In a recent development, we love that both the main vacuum head and pet hair attachment come with headlights because it makes it a lot easier to see hidden dirt and debris. The brush roll is a tangle-free design, and the FurFinder is equipped with a HEPA filter for trapping small particles and allergens.

The motor on this vacuum is less powerful than the PowerClean, but it still provides plenty of suction for daily household cleaning.

Full Bissell PowerClean FurFinder Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

Since we’re major fans of the Shark AZ2002 Vertex upright vacuum for deep and thorough cleans, it’s no surprise that we like the cordless model in this lineup, too. The brush roll is excellent at pulling hair and large debris from carpets, as well as polishing up your hardwood floors. The cordless stick vacuum features an advertised runtime of 60 minutes.

It also offers a HEPA filtration system and converts to a hand vac, and it also bends at the center of the wand to get around and under furniture. The Vertex comes with plenty of accessories for cleaning a variety of spaces. However, this may not be the best choice if you regularly clean stairs, as the cordless vacuum weighs roughly nine pounds—significantly more than other vacuums we cover.

I have two cats and live with my partner, which means there is plenty of mess to go around, from pet hair and dust to tracked-in dirt. I appreciate all the thoughtful features of the Tineco Station 5 because they make daily maintenance much easier.

Automatic suction adjustment has proved useful on my laminate and tile floors. I can hear when the motor gets a boost of power in a particularly dirty area, and it helps on carpets and area rugs where crumbs and debris tends to get trapped between the fibers. Add to that a green laser light for dust detection and you’ll hardly ever miss a spot.

Recent findings suggest that I particularly like the base station. It has a 2.5-liter capacity, and after two months of using the Station 5, I still haven’t had to empty it. When I dock the vacuum onto the base, it automatically empties the onboard dustbin, cleans the floorhead brush roll, and charges the vacuum. Combined, these intuitive features make for a cleaning routine that is virtually hands-free.

Full Tineco Pure ONE Station 5 Pro Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

Even though the Dyson V11 Origin came out several years ago, that doesn’t mean this model has stopped being useful.

The motorbar cleaner head works exceptionally well on carpet, successfully agitating fibers to pull up embedded dirt, dander, and hair. Suction is equally impressive, and there are three power modes depending on the level of cleaning you need. I ran the vacuum on medium most of the time, but I used boost occasionally whenever an area needed the extra attention.

This model doesn’t come with a soft roller brush vacuum head, and while it does work on all floor types, it can be loud on hardwood and laminate. But if your home is mostly carpet, this is a cordless stick vacuum I would reach for.

Full Dyson V11 Origin Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

In a recent development, our tester has a busy household six pets, so there’s no question that she’s regularly cleaning up after her animals. Pulling out the upright vacuum daily isn’t convenient, so she turned to the Levoit LVAC-300 to fill the gap.

This cordless stick vacuum has three different cleaning modes—eco, medium, and max—and she was able to cycle through each right from the handle depending on how much suction power she needed. She found that the vacuum was able to pick up litter and sand on different surfaces and between thresholds with ease.

According to recent reports, the attachments are useful for cleaning curtains, cushions, and staircases, but she was disappointed that there’s nowhere to store these tools on the vacuum itself. The LVAC-300 runs for up to 60 minutes depending on what mode you’re using, and the HEPA filter is a great feature if you have animals.

Full Levoit LVAC-300 Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

I used the Bissell PowerClean FurGuard across my apartment to clean laminate floors, area rugs, carpeting, and upholstery, and I fell in love with several features.

It has been revealed that the vacuum lays completely flat, making it really easy to get underneath furniture, and the swivel steering helps guide the FurGuard around tight spaces. Being a pet owner, I appreciate that the brush roll is tangle-free, so I don’t have to cut hair loose as often as I would with a standard, bristled brush roll.

Other highlights were lights on the main vacuum head and pet hair attachment. I was able to see collected dirt and debris that I would normally miss on hardwood flooring, carpet, and furniture. I also like that this model is designed to be self-standing.

It’s hard to come by a cordless stick vacuum that you don’t have to re-mount or set on the ground during your cleaning session. With this model, I was able to stop and start with ease.

Full Bissell PowerClean FurGuard Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

In a recent development, we recently got our hands on one of the latest cordless stick vacuums from Shark, and we were impressed by the PowerDetect’s construction. The pole has a hinge in the center and when you release it, the vacuum bends to extend under furniture and hard-to-reach places. Our tester didn’t have to kneel down or adjust angles while he was cleaning thanks to the intuitive design.

In a recent development, beyond that, the PowerDetect vacuum uses sensors on the bottom of the floor head to discern between surface types, and adjusts suction power when needed. During testing, the motor could be heard transitioning speeds when used on hardwood and shag carpet.

Recent findings suggest that this vacuum also comes with a docking station, which automates the process of emptying out the dustbin. The vacuum itself can’t hold that much debris onboard, so it’s nice having a one-stop-shop for clearing out the bagless canister during a cleaning session. It’s a little heavy for a cordless stick vacuum, but it still gets the job done.

Full Shark PowerDetect Cordless Stick Vacuum Review.

It has been revealed that not every cordless stick vacuum we test ends up in this roundup. However, these other models still perform well and are reliable recommendations:.

According to recent reports, levoit Aero Cordless Vacuum Cleaner: The Tineco we’ve included above has more raw suction power, reaching up to 27,000Pa versus the 14,000Pa of the Levoit. However, one of the highlights of the Aero is the 3.5-liter-capacity dust bag in the docking station. Depending on your cleaning frequency, you could potentially go months without having to empty and replace it, and this design is better for keeping dust and dander from being expelled back into the air.

Dyson Gen5Detect Cordless Stick Vacuum: This cordless stick vacuum certainly commands a premium price, and you get a lot of the same features as the Dyson V15 Detect we recommend above, such as an LCD display screen, the Fluffy Optic cleaner head, and pet hair attachments. If you’re an allergy sufferer, you may prefer the Gen5Detect because its filtration system captures particles down to 0.1 microns, while the V15 filters down to just 0.3 microns. Plus, runtime is slightly longer on the Gen5Detect.

The main advantages of owning a cordless stick vacuum are easy portability and storage. But what you trade for the convenience is battery life and runtime. Most models clean from 30 to 60 minutes, but that’s also dependent on what setting you’re using. If you’re running the vacuum on its highest speed the entire time, it might die faster. Be wary of manufacturers’ advertised total runtime because it may represent performance on the lowest setting or using two fully charged batteries, for instance. Battery charging should also be factored in, so blueprint your cleaning session accordingly so you don’t lose power in the middle of a floor swipe.

Industry observers note that like we mentioned earlier, the dustbins on cordless stick vacuums are significantly smaller than those of an upright or canister unit. You should consider your cleaning habits and the spaces you usually vacuum to find a model that aligns with your needs. If you live in an apartment or are using the cordless vac to supplement your other cleaning supplies, then a dustbin with at least half a liter capacity should do. Some of the models we recommend hold up to one liter of debris, which helps limit the number of trips to the trash can.

Although not a necessity, having a good amount of attachments with your vacuum is especially helpful for cleaning hard-to-reach places or targeting specific issues. Crevice tools pick up dirt and dander from corners and couch cushions, while bristled brushes and motorized pet tools agitate and lift hair and fur that’s been embedded into upholstery.

A good filtration system helps combat allergens such as dust and pet dander that are being kicked up by a vacuum. The best option is a HEPA filter, or “high-efficiency particulate air” filter, which traps 99.97 percent of particles that are 0.3 microns or larger in size. A fully sealed or multi-step filtration system also has the potential to trap a wide variety of airborne allergens without releasing them back into your home.

Cordless vacuums are very effective at picking up pet hair, especially models designed with high suction power and specialized brush rolls. Some of the models we recommend include motorized attachments that lift embedded hair from upholstery and carpets. Anti-tangle vacuum heads are also a key feature that helps prevent hair from wrapping around the brush roll. While not all models perform equally, a high-quality cordless stick vacuum is able to handle pet hair just as well as traditional versions.

The lifespan of these vacuums typically lasts from three to five years, depending on usage, build quality, and maintenance. Battery performance plays a major role, since lithium-ion batteries start to lose capacity over time.

In a recent development, avoiding overcharging and storing the vacuum properly could help extend the battery life significantly. Running regular maintenance like cleaning the vacuum filters and emptying the dustbin completely preserves suction and functionality. Higher-end models often last longer due to better materials and replaceable parts, but either price point has potential to last for years with proper care.

Modern designs are increasingly more effective at cleaning many surface types, including rugs and carpets. Advances in battery tech and general efficiency have allowed for strong suction performance that is comparable to corded models. Adjustable power modes allow for deeper cleaning on thicker carpets, and multi-roller and motorized brush heads agitate fibers to loosen dirt and debris.

Performance may vary depending on the type of flooring. Some vacuums are designed to work on low-to-medium pile carpets, while others are able to handle high-pile. It’s best to consult the listed features and specs of the model you’re considering to ensure it aligns with the flooring types in your home.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the future of 84 KFC and KFC/Taco Bell restaurants across 10 states is uncertain after one of the chain’s franchisees filed for bankruptcy. The operator, Tasty Chick’n, filed for Chapter 11 protection in Texas on November 16.

Industry observers note that the firm entered into franchise agreements in 2021 with KFC and Taco Bell, both owned by Yum! Brands. Tasty Chick’n’s portfolio includes 75 KFC restaurants and nine co-branded locations across Tennessee, Florida, Virginia, Arkansas, Kentucky, Illinois, Missouri, Alabama, Mississippi, and Indiana.

In its bankruptcy filing, Tasty Chick’n notes that sales have declined by 15.6 percent over the past three fiscal years while operating costs have skyrocketed. So far in 2026, restaurant-level profit margins have dropped to just 4 percent, down from 11 percent in 2023. And under its franchise agreements, nearly half of the franchisees’ locations require substantial and expensive upgrades through 2029.

Tasty Chick’n began deferring royalty payments in mid-2025 and generally stopped paying them altogether that November. This past September, KFC and Taco Bell’s franchising entities issued a notice of intent to terminate their agreements, claiming the operator owed nearly $16 million in unpaid royalties and other fees. Tasty Chick’n also faces approximately 14 lawsuits from landlords in five states over unpaid rent and other charges. The bankruptcy filing revealed that the operator has accrued nearly $73 million in funded debt.

Recent findings suggest that the fate of the restaurants remains undecided. Tasty Chick’n is planning a court-supervised sale of its portfolio, either in its entirety or divided into different regional markets. Whether buyers will bite is another story, especially given KFC’s overall trajectory. A report earlier this year revealed that KFC had shuttered more than 300 locations between July 2025 and July 2026 alone.

No matter what happens to these KFC locations, this bankruptcy is another reminder of just how tough 2026 has been for fast food operators.

Imagine a Parker House roll having a tryst with Asian-style milk bread and a classic French croissant—that’s the essence of salt bread, a.k.a. shio pan in Japan and sogeum-ppang in Korea.

Sources indicate that “These little buns…they look so cute, but they are so rich,” guest contributor, and our deputy food editor, Hana Asbrink explains to BA Bake Club hosts Jesse Szewczyk and Shilpa Uskokovic. “You can really just snack on them solo and be so satisfied.”.

According to recent reports, this month’s episode is also more bittersweet than usual, as Shilpa reveals that she is leaving Bon Appétit to take on latest projects. “I’m so proud of Bake Club,” Shilpa says. “Thank you to all of our readers and listeners. You really have made this the most wholesome corner of the internet and my career.”.

We can’t let her go without a proper send off. Follow Shilpa on Instagram to see what comes next in her baking adventures. And fret not, BA Bake Club will continue full steam ahead with Jesse at the helm!

We’d love to hear from you! Send your questions to BA Bake Club on Substack or send a voice memo or email to [email protected].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that delish editors handpick every product we feature. We may earn commission from the links on this page.

The day before Thanksgiving is getting even more epic than usual. On November 25, Hershey’s is traveling back in time to when the manufacturer first released its iconic Milk Chocolate Bars. Back in 1900, the bars sold for just five cents a piece, and for one day only, the company is bringing back that original price.

Timed to coincide with the November 25 release of Hershey, a film about founder Milton Hershey starring Finn Wittrock and Alexandra Daddario, the super-discounted chocolate bars make for the perfect stocking stuffer or post-Thanksgiving treat.

In a recent development, there are a few ways to score the deal, although the rules vary depending on where you're shopping. Starting at 9 a.m. EST, customers can purchase the five-cent chocolate bars through Walmart.com for online pickup with a Walmart account. The offer is also available in stores through the Ibotta app, where shoppers must first purchase a bar at regular price and submit their receipt to receive cash back. Both options have a five-bar limit per person.

Sources indicate that the bars will also be available through Amazon Grocery for same-day delivery where available. Hershey's will also share a promo code on its social channels for free shipping to qualifying addresses. Amazon purchases are limited to two bars per person, and additional fees for non-Prime members and taxes may apply.

Lucky visitors to Hershey's Chocolate World in Hershey, Pennsylvania, and Times Square in New York City can also enjoy the deal, starting at 9 a.m. and 10 a.m., respectively. Purchases at these locations are limited to 10 bars per person while supplies last, and taxes may apply.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the midst of a rich meal, something fresh and acidic keeps your taste buds awake. Where lettuce splashed with vinaigrette can feel like an afterthought, a juicy, savory-slanting pear salad is worth making room for on a plate full of turkey and cornbread. This is the antithesis of the haphazardly chunked together fruit salads you find at the supermarket for a brunch or dessert spread. Keep the focus on crisp-tart pears—apples also work—and it’s a welcome accompaniment to the other hearty dishes. Sliced razor-thin (use a mandoline) and fanned out on a platter, the fruit acts as an edible canvas for wisps of cheese and clusters of honey-roasted seeds. Leftovers (if you have any, of course) are delightful spooned over a well-toasted and buttered slice of multigrain bread the next day.

In a recent development, pick firm green pears (Bartlett and Anjou are fair game; use Asian pears in a pinch) to ensure they hold their shape once sliced—even a little underripe is better than slightly over. After slicing, have a taste: If they are very tart, add 1 tsp. honey to the dressing; if fairly sweet, skip it.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

It has been revealed that preheat oven to 325°. Whisk 3 Tbsp. honey, 1 tsp. garlic powder, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine. Add 1 cup raw sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or coarsely crushed raw nuts (such as walnuts, almonds, and/or hazelnuts) and stir to coat. Spread out in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet; reserve bowl.

Bake seed mixture until golden brown, 12–14 minutes. (Honey mixture will puff up a bit but will deflate when you stir.) Toss honey-roasted seeds, then let cool. Toss again just to break up.

Recent findings suggest that whisk 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp. Dijon mustard, a pinch of kosher salt, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in reserved bowl. Add 2 lb. firm green pears (such as Bartlett and/or Anjou; about 4 large), cored, thinly sliced, to dressing and gently toss to coat.

Recent findings suggest that arrange pears on a large flat platter. Scatter honey-roasted seeds over and top with 2 oz. Parmesan, aged white cheddar, or Manchego cheese, shaved.

Do Ahead: Honey-roasted seeds can be made 6 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.
